If you are going to allow physical play, the ref cannot call that foul on Estupian. Such garbage

Amorim must know by now that rotating 5-6 players each match will lead to inconsistency and will ultimately get him fired. Today was a win with the right players on the pitch. And the right players in the stands.

From October 11th up until today, November 8th, Milan played 9 games in 28 days. Let that sink in before you try to complain about rotations. Also, outside of Torriani and Bartesaghi all other players that played vs Ferencvaros played today. “Torriani and Bartesaghi all other players that played vs Ferencvaros played today.”

Happy Ramos got an assist cuz he was vital to both goals, so often he makes the decoy run to open space for the 2nd runner. With better service he’d score plenty himself, but we dont create many good chances at all. Terra also did much better today, definitely crucial to keeping the 3 points.

Milan exaggeration in playing in the back almost lost them the game. I dont understand why its so difficult for Milan in the last decade to build quick attacks. Nonetheless, 3 points earned. I hope the manager can fix these observations and realize the fans like a fierce Milan.

#1564. Allegri banned for Juventus reunion as Napoli lodge appeal

Massimiliano Allegri will not be on the Napoli bench when his side visit the Allianz Stadium on Sunday night. Serie A’s sporting judge has suspended the former Juventus coach for two matches following his dismissal against Roma, although Napoli have confirmed they will challenge the decision.

The ban means one of the most talked about reunions of the autumn could take place without its main character in the dugout, unless the appeal goes Napoli’s way before the weekend.

Allegri was sent off late in Saturday’s 3-3 draw with Roma at the Maradona, reacting furiously after Leonardo Balerdi struck a late equaliser for the visitors. As Football Italia reported, he removed his jacket and walked away before returning and having to be held back by his own staff.

The judge’s ruling, published on Monday and detailed by Sky Sport Italia, goes further than the touchline incident. Allegri was punished for an insulting remark aimed at the match officials in the 90th minute, a seriously disrespectful comment directed at them in the dressing room area afterwards, and aggressive behaviour towards an executive of the opposing club. The first two were noted by the fourth official and the referee, the last by staff working for the federal prosecutor.

On top of the suspension, the 59-year-old has been fined €10,000.

The two games Allegri is set to miss are both away from home. Napoli travel to Monza in the midweek round on Wednesday 28 October, before heading to Turin to face Juventus on Sunday 1 November, with both matches kicking off at 20:45 local time.

If the ban stands, his first game back on the bench would be the home fixture against Lazio on Sunday 8 November.

Official SSC Napoli (@sscnapoli) October 26, 2026

Napoli moved quickly. In a short club statement on Monday afternoon, the Partenopei said that, having requested access to the official documents, they would lodge an appeal against the two match suspension handed to their coach.

Sky Sport Italia notes that a successful appeal would open the door for Allegri to take his place on the bench in Turin. Italian reports suggest the case should be heard before the end of the week, so the picture ought to be clear before Sunday.

For Juventus supporters, any meeting with Allegri carries extra weight. He led the club across two spells, the second of which ended in May 2024, and he remains one of the most successful coaches in its history.

Luciano Spalletti’s side head into the week in a better mood after ending a 35 day wait for a league win with the 2-0 victory at Lecce, which lifted them to seventh on 14 points. Douglas Luiz was among the scorers that night, as covered in our report on his first goal for the club.

Whether or not Allegri is in the dugout, Napoli will arrive as a dangerous opponent. You can follow every twist in his relationship with the Bianconeri on our Massimiliano Allegri page.

Sources: Sky Sport Italia, SSC Napoli, Football Italia

#1563. Man United news: New manager 'favourite' other than Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann amid Michael Carrick sack pressure

By Lewis Nolan | 08 Nov 2026 23:47

Mauricio Pochettino has joined the likes of Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann as favourites to replace Manchester United boss Michael Carrick.

The Red Devils earned a point in their final Premier League game before the start of the international break, with the club drawing 4-4 with Aston Villa on Sunday.

Carrick's side came back from 2-0 and 4-2 deficits to avoid defeat, though the result left the team in 18th place, and their placement has fuelled calls for a change in the dugout.

A number of managers have been linked with Old Trafford, including former Newcastle boss Howe and former Bayern Munich head coach Nagelsmann.

However, the Evening Standard have claimed that current USA national team coach Pochettino has emerged as a leading contender should Carrick lose his job.

Most United supporters will remember Pochettino from his time at Tottenham Hotspur, with the 54-year-old spending five years at the club between 2014 and 2019.

While he failed to win a trophy in London, the Argentine managed to reach the 2014-15 EFL Cup final, as well as the 2018-19 Champions League final, while he guided the club to two third-placed finishes, one second-placed finish and one fourth-placed finish.

It should be noted that Pochettino was dealing with a restricted transfer budget for much of his time at Spurs, yet he created one of the most exciting teams in the division, getting the most out of stars like Harry Kane, Dele Alli, Christian Eriksen and Son Heung-min.

Failed spells at Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea following his exit from Tottenham in 2019 should not overshadow his qualities as a coach, and if he can get the Red Devils to play as energetically as his Spurs side did, then United will be a threat against most opponents.

Even though there may be some concerns about Pochettino's ability to get the club over the line in the biggest moments, United are not in a position to turn down someone with the track record of the Argentine.

No other team have won fewer games in the Premier League this season than United (one), and the club are only one point above last-placed Crystal Palace.

The Red Devils are set for a difficult test against Liverpool at Anfield after the international break, and heading into that game without fundamental changes could be disastrous.

Many fans are fond of Carrick for his contributions as a player at Old Trafford, and perhaps now would be the best time to dismiss him with the chance to walk away after a spirited comeback rather than a potentially devastating result against the Merseysiders.

#1562. Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon

The noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half. It was muffled at first, but as the ball popped from one white shirt to another, it became louder and louder, sweeping around the stadium: here was the soundtrack for a humiliation.

“Olé! Olé! Olé!” they roared and why not? Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins. Football has become a sport that leaves people increasingly vexed, but this was a night when – for the locals, at least – it was almost a throwback.

There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.

“I suppose in football you can always find something to moan about,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, said. “But this was a top-class performance.”

It has felt suspiciously like Newcastle’s start has been like an overstuffed plastic shopping bag, the handles straining to the point of snapping. Eventually they fell asunder. Leeds ran all over them and were too smart, slick and hungry, not to mention ruthless. No wonder Jaissle had nowhere to go.

The home fans were adamant this was one of the best nights Leeds have experienced under Farke and if they were prepared to say as much, you had an obligation to listen. Forget how wretched Newcastle were, Leeds had produced a performance to enable imaginations to run wild.

Centre to it all was Ao Tanaka, with his desire to keep Leeds playing forward, but it felt wrong to talk about one man when you had the unstoppable Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who would be substituted to a standing ovation, and the ubiquitous James Justin, among others.

"He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj

The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous new West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a big evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Big? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

Jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO

Leeds were running even quicker by this point, pressing as if their lives depended on it and making tackles that were lustily acclaimed in the stands. Steur completely short-circuited in the bedlam and a ridiculous pass on the edge of his area was pounced upon by Bogle.

Out went a ball to Justin, whose cross was whipped into the penalty area, where Calvert-Lewin had climbed to get his head to it, though replays indicated his effort glanced off Bogle’s head – determining the true scorer will make for an interesting conversation.

Calvert-Lewin, at least, got the reward his efforts deserved on the cusp of half-time, spinning away from Miley and chopping inside Sven Botman before delivering the kind of finish that should make Thomas Tuchel take note when selecting his next England squad this week.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9

The gloss, after those “olés”, was applied in the 59th minute when Noah Okafor put a realistic hue on the score, ramming in a finish in front of the Kop and leaving Newcastle open to the crudest mocking for the amount of money they have spent to resemble such a disorganised rabble.

A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x

Bazoumana Touré, at least, scored a consolation goal, but Jaissle barely flickered as it went in and the emotion belonged to Farke, who thundered on to the pitch at the final whistle and sought out his captain, Ampadu, who had erred in allowing Newcastle’s substitute to profit.

“That was an unnecessary goal to concede and I so wanted us to keep a clean sheet,” Farke sighed. “We deserved a clean sheet and I couldn’t help myself. I had to tell him because I am sometimes a perfectionist. We must try to stay humble, but we can be an outstanding team.”

And this, for certain, was an outstanding night.

[It was brutal out there?] That’s football. That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have said it many times. We will have ups and downs and challenges all the way. Tonight we faced that challenge. It’s tough and difficult to digest. But there is a chance to learn out of that and there’s a long time until our next match at home and that is good.

It’s clear with our young squad that there will be ups and downs and you have to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against such a physical team. Leeds are so intense, we couldn’t match that physicality. There are other aspects of course but I don’t want to make excuses. We want to learn out of it and be better.

[Were you overwhelmed as a team?] No. If you don’t bring that physicality on the pitch, you struggle.

Exactly this [message to the players]. Bring your fundamentals and we build on it. [Can you bounce back from this in your next game?] Of course. [Is your confidence hit?] No

For each manager it would be a nightmare after such a game to concede so late and not have the well-deserved clean sheet. Of course I was not happy about the situation. Doesn’t take anything away from my boys who were magnificent. Terrific start with eight points but there’s never a perfect performance. There’s always something to moan about. At very rare points [in the season] I have to criticise [for conceding].

Energy, quality, good structure, in an out of possession, which is complicated against Newcastle, In pressing them you always have to be aware of their unbelievable pace and strength in counter-attacks. We found this balance today and in the first half particularly we were dominant.

We have a good fitness level now. Need to find the right triggers to press. It’s a lot of well-structured work on the training ground. We had more chances to score tonight but overall I am very happy with our performance.

[Calvert-Lewin being praised] It is well deserved. He is in outstanding shape and plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group with some other players. His work-rate is never in doubt and to me he is one of the best strikers in the league.

The ref told me at half-time that they’ve taken it off me. I didn’t know he [Bogle] was there to be fair. I just got up and went ‘Bang!’ It is what it is. I’ll take the assist!

I didn’t know anything about it [being given credit for the second goal]. I said to the ref, I don’t fancy telling him [Calvert-Lewin]. To be fair he’s still raging. He’s raging with the goal but happy with the result.

It’s about having an understanding with the players around you. With Dom up there, you know he’s going to win everything so you have to get the runners around him.

It’s about the rotation like today. When James Justin goes wider there’s space inside. Dom occupies two centre-backs so there’s always pockets.

Regardless of the scoreline it was a tough game physically. They’re a very good side. We take it game by game, not to get carried away. Everyone’s ambitious in their own way but we have to take it game by game.

A proper stuffing for Newcastle as Leeds continue to impress and climb up to third.

Newcastle corner on the left headed out by Elvedi and Barnes recovers the ball to start another attack with the 18-yard line stacked with players. When the diagonal comes back from left to right Barnes heads it behind for a goalkick.

Newcastle free-kick for a trip on Willock. Hall takes and Leeds head it out for a throw-in.

Livramento improves the quality of crosses with two that at least find the middle of the box even if they were headed away by Elvedi and Justin respectively.

Newcastle are enjoying more possession but the crossing has been awful when they do get down the flanks, Touré the latest offender.

Barnes shoots down Trafford’s throat. Barnes had thrown himself down in the box moments earlier and there was a VAR check but there was nothing like the contact required to send him swan-diving on to the grass.

Wissa gets down the right and whips over a low cross but Willock’s touch was too heavy.

There was a piece in the Athletic today saying Newcastle pivoted to Hornicek instead of pursuing Trafford again because he had a very high ceiling and was younger. He hasn’t caught much here, dropping the ball even when he chooses not to punch.

Matthias Jaissle promised high intensity, high octane, front foot football when he was interviewed for the Newcastle job. He and sporting director Ross Wilson have repeated that promise several times since he was appointed. There has been no sign of it since the opening weekend against Liverpool.

Newcastle are passive, they look disorganised in midfield and weak at the back. Oh and they barely apply pressure let alone attack dangerously.

These are early days but this performance and result had been coming. A pretty brutal reality check after all the positive noise and bold predictions in pre-season. This defeat will drop Newcastle to 12th in the table, where they finished last season under Eddie Howe.

Leeds 4 Newcastle 0 (Okafor) Ampadu hurls it into the box. A defender heads it to the edge of the area where Okafor thumps a left-footed half-volley in off the right post.

A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x

Livramento slides in to stop Okafor’s drive down the left, giving Leeds another opportunity to throw it long.

Triple change: Livramento → DedicTouré → Fernandez-PardoWillock → Murphy

Leeds catch Newcastle playing short from the back. Stach blindsides Steur 20 yards out, tackles him, cuts inside then bends a left foot shot into the side-netting.

After Hall stings Trafford’s palms with a strike from distance. Newcastle want a penalty when the ball hits Tanaka’s arm … but it was outside the area and then Murphy, in frustration, chops down Gudmundsson and takes the booking as an occupational hazard.

Elvedi sloppily gives the ball way to Wissa who tries to set Fernandez-Pardo through down the left. Justin sticks with him and Bogle mops up after Justin was tripped.

Gudmundsson does the upended beetle when he tries to break from the corner and collides with a Newcastle player. He claims he was fouled and wthrashes about like a RL player after he’s tackled. He continues to do a Rumpelstiltskin polka of peevishness towards the ref for a while.

Newcastle corner on the left that Trafford backpedals to tip behind for another.

No changes at half-time for Newcastle as they kick off. Leeds break through the middle quickly and Calvert-Lewin seems to push the ball past Botman and shapes to shoot before Steur slides in with a crucial tackle just inside the box.

The first goal is now an own goal. The explanation is that Tanaka’s shot was on target but the deflection from Steur meant it was going wide until it hit Miley.

Now the second goal has been credited to Bogle as Calvert-Lewin’s header struck the top of his head before it went in.

You could not say that this scoreline is undeserved. Newcastle are being demolished physically. The central midfield two – Steur and Miley – just don’t have the power to screen their defence.

Leeds 3 Newcastle 0 (Calvert-Lewin) Leeds are running all over Newcastle who seem physically flimsy. Calvert-Lewin chops in from the left on to a flick-on, the ball takes a deflection off the Newcastle captain and he steers it into the far corner with a right-foot shot.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9

Calvert-Lewin is booked for catching Botman in the face with a straight arm rather than a swinging arm. ‘Reckless but not violent.’ Trafford had punchd the corner away at the back post to set Leeds off on a counter.

Tanaka gives the ball away carelessly in midfield and Newcastle work it to Wissa who chops inside past Elvedi, hangs out his own leg looking for contact and hits the deck. The ref waves play on and the ball runs to Barnes in the left of the area. He shapes to shoot but Muharemovic sprinted over to make a fine block-tackle, forcing it behind for a corner.

Newcastle are rocking here. They cannot win a tackle.

For those of us who have watched all Newcastle United’s games this season, this was coming. They do not have any consistent attacking threat, they do no create chances and they are not secure at the back either.

They’ve survived by converting the very few chances they create in games but they have not even had a shot in the first half here.

Leeds should be three up after Hornicek fumbled Gudmundsson’s shot from the left. The ball falls to Calvert-Lewin five yards out and he triesto dink it over the keeper who recovers well to smother it.

Leeds 2 Newcastle 0 (Calvert-Lewin) Newcastle try to play the ball out from the back, give it away cheaply to Bogle who feeds Justin haring down the right. He is ostensibly the right centre-back but he is a full-back by trade and stands up a perfect near-post cross that Calvert-Lewin hangs in the air to bury with the firmest of headers. In fact it transpires that his downward header struck Bogle and another deflection benefits rampant Leeds –162 seconds between the goals.

"He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj

Leeds 1 Newcastle 0 (Tanaka) Good move, spawny finish. Tanaka sprays a pass out to Okafor who drives at Dedic then picks out Tanaka who had held his run. He cushions the pass then lets fly. The ball hits Steur, deflects on to Miley and then loops into the right of the goal with Hornicek understandably stranded.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO

Good tackle by Steur on Bogle stops the Leeds right-back flying forward after Calvert-Lewin’s flick-on.

Newcastle really are not afraid to launch the ball forward are they? Football tactics are constantly evolving and fashions come back around. What better way to play through a press than to bypass the midfield completely? The hope is it will also cause the centre-backs problems, get them facing their own goal under pressure from one of Newcastle’s rapid forward players in a foot race.

It almost worked a couple of times in the first half but it should be pointed out that the best direct/long ball teams of the past tended to have a striker who was dominant in the air. Newcastle do not currently have one which does limit their threat from flick ons.

Newcastle break from defending a long throw. Wissa carries it 60 yards but with Murphy and Fernadez-Pardo better placed, he tries to shoot from 25 yards and plinks it straight at Trafford, provoking an inevitable ‘Woooooooo’.

From the resulting long throw Elvedi is found at the back post, unmarked and attempts to volley it towards goal, missing the ball entirely. It was so wild that even the Leeds staff laugh at how inept it was.

Leeds have a corner when they use one of their signature moves, Bogle cutting in from the right across the back four to take a ball over the top. He controls it but cannot force it past Thiaw.

Hornicek claws out the corner to Bogle 18 yards out. He puts his laces through a volley that Hornicek parries up high and punches away when he has a second go.

Newcastle chip it long again, this time down the right. Gudmundsson holds off Murphy and Leeds will have the relief of a goal-kick.

Leeds are finding it hard now to play through Newcastle’s high press and the intensity with which they are hounding keeper and defenders.

Newcastle keep looking to use their pace with balls over the top for Wissa, Murphy and Fernandez-Pardo. Wissa closes Trafford down quickly again. He needs to release it with more urgency.

Gonzalez hs not recovered from being struck on the head by the ball and is being replaced by Steur as a concussion sub.

Justin heads over his own bar when Newcastle chip a long pass down the inside right. Wissa beats Muharemovic and tries to find Fernandez-Pardo but Justin got there first. Newcastle go short from the corner and Leeds force them back into their own half.

Terrific save from Hornicek down low to his right. Tanaka’s cross from the left found Justin creeping round the back on the right and heading across goal from the back post. Bogle swivelled and tried a sidewinder flick that was arrowing towards the bottom left corner until the keeper swooped to turn it away with his right hand.

Wissa is ticking, feeling he is getting nothing from the referee when challenging for the ball, the latest incident involving a collision with Justin which was 50-50.

Leeds have been the slicker of the two sides, their passing and movement causing the full-backs problems. Okafor dribbles down the left and centres. Stach lays it back to Ampadu who hammers a half-volley from 18 yards that poleaxes Calvert-Lewin who was in an offside position.

Newcastle fans sing ‘There’s only one Kevin Keegan’ as the visitors’ defence sweeps the ball around. When they knock the ball up the inisde-right channel Wissa is penalised for swinging his arm and catching Muharemovic in the mooey.

Wissa presses Trafford high and the goalkeeper is a bit too casual but gets away with it. His clearance bounces off the attacker’s shin and loops out to the right. Leeds shift it quickly out to the left with Gudmundsson and Okafor bombing forward. A vicious cross from the left-back hits a Newcastle leg, loops up and smaxks Gonzales flush in the face, knocking him off his feet. The ref stops play.

Two bad moments for Newcastle early on. Lewis Hall caught out by a simple run and pass behind him and then, from the resulting corner Mathias Fernandez-Pardo looked very fortunate, in my opinion, to avoid conceding a penalty for handball.

He got the benefit of the doubt presumably because the ball bounced up onto his hand as he tried to bring it under control and he did not intend to control it with his hand or knock it away. The handball law confuses me but there is a higher threshold now.

Stach tackles Wissa in the centre-circle. Wissa is playing behind Fernandez-Pardo. Ampadu receives a long pass over the top, coming back from an offside position in the nick of time.

Fernandez-Pardo’s outstretched left arm is struck in the penalty area with the ball after they win the header but the ref waves play on and stops the game for a foul on the new striker.

It’s never a problem to come to Elland Road and the singing of Marching On Together before kick-off makes this one of the top three atmospheres in the country, easily. There are problems with VAR, though, and the whole stadium has just seen the ball strike Matias Fernanzes-Pardo’s hand in the area. The reason it is a problem is because we have become conditioned to thinking every time a ball touches someone on the arm in the area, a penalty should be awarded. It is preposterous that faceless beaks have distorted the game so much.

Leeds kick off, attacking the South Stand, from left to right, as they always prefer to do. Justin and Bogle combine on the right and Bogle bends a pass inside HAll to Stach who chooses to cross rather than shoot. It hits Botman and goes out for a corner.

Leeds are in their home kit of white with yellow and blue pinstripe hoops, Newcastle in their navy away kit.

Anthony [Elanga] is injured. Unfortunately we have to investigate further how long he will be out but obviously we miss him. We wish him to come back as quickly as possible. It could be [a long-term injury] but he will get another MRI next week and then we’ll see.

Lewis Hall is the perfect player profile for how we play. he is a young lad still and we are very excited [that he has signed a new contract].

The start was not easy. We didn’t have lots of time to prepare for pre-season and that’s one reason we are happy and satisfied with the start. But there is potential and we will work hard on the margins we want to improve.

There will be a lot of excitement surrounding Mathias Fernandez-Pardo’s first start for Newcastle United following his deadline day move from Lille but also keep an eye on Jacob Murphy on the right wing.

Fernandez-Pardo starts with a clean slate at Newcastle, Murphy has a lot of baggage and he has been a popular online target for criticism over the last year or so.

Indeed, some sections of the fanbase were stunned Newcastle rejected a £15m offer from Nottingham Forest on deadline day for a player who has entered the final 12 months of his contract.

Murphy has his limitations, sure and he can be infuriating sometimes when he gives the ball away cheaply, but there is a reason Matthias Jaissle was adamant he could not be sold.

Part of that is due to the fact he does not have another specialist right winger behind Anthony Elanga who misses the Leeds game through injury.

But Murphy is also valued for his experience and his training ground presence. He has been at the club a long time, working under Rafa Benítez, Steve Bruce and Eddie Howe and is a boyhood Newcastle fan.

Jaissle was not willing to lose that from his dressing room. Ultimately, though, Murphy has to perform on the pitch to justify the faith shown in him.

There are not many other options to fill that position while Elanga is missing. Harvey Barnes does not like playing on the right, Amar Dedic is a full back and so is Tino Livramento.

This is an opportunity for Murphy to silence his detractors and prove the faith Jaissle has put in him is not misplaced. At the age of 31, he knows he is not the most popular or appreciated player at the club but he has never shirked or complained about that.

He formed a potent partnership with Alexander Isak when he was leading the line for Newcastle. Can he do the same with the new boy Fernandez-Pardo?

Mind you I remember his visit to Elland Road in 1982-83. Not for the faint hearted. In fact it was a disgrace when he was hit by a coin. And yet he was always gracious about Leeds and particularly fond of Don Revie. He was one of very few football people without a strong Leeds United connection who went to his funeral in 1989.

Apparently he was injured in training, the nature of the injury is unspecified.

Newcastle have made a very good start particularly in their transitional moments on the counter-attack. We have to be switched on today to get the next points.

After many years of suffering our supporters deserve it [high expectations]. It’s good but we are far away from not being humble. Our feet are on the ground. We know the second year is always difficult. We have made a good start and it is always important to ride the momentum as long as possible.

Eddie Howe has left a legacy and the culture he created is still around. Matthias has to work with it. They are unbeaten. they are very dangerous with many pacy players up front. It’s important not to lose the ball too easily and always be switched on against Newcastle.

Leeds United Trafford; Justin, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Bogle, Ampadu, Tanaka, Gudmundsson; Stach, Okafor; Calvert-Lewin. Substitutes Zetterer, Bard, Bijol, Longstaff, Aaronson, Wilson, James, Bahoya, Nmecha.

Newcastle United (4-2-3-1) Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; González, L Miley; Murphy, Fernandez-Pardo, Barnes; Wissa. Substitutes Pope, Livramento, Schär, Bamba, Steur, Touré, Willock, Ramsey, M Miley.

MFP starts at Elland Road! 🇧🇪 pic.twitter.com/b3Gsazcuaf

Farke names same side as the starting XI for the 1-1 draw with Brighton:

📋 Your #LUFC XI... pic.twitter.com/FG3gW13U8S

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Leeds United vs Newcastle United, the last Premier League match of the fourth round of fixtures for the 2026-27 season. Both clubs have made unbeaten starts with one win and two draws each and a win today for wither would send them up to fourth. The two sides met at Elland Road in the third match of last season which ended in a 0-0 draw but the return fixture at St James’ Park was one of the games of the season, a ding-dong match that Leeds led 0-1, 1-2 and 2-3, the latter until the 91st minute and yet still lost 4-3.

The architect of that victory for Newcastle was the Leeds’ fans’ incubus, a player commonly known around Elland Road as ‘Harvey F------- Barnes’. His two goals that night were his sixth and seventh against Leeds in eight matches for Leicester and the Toon. Back in the last century and at the turn of this one, Alan Shearer scored 21 league goals in 23 games against Leeds for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle, it can feel like one bogeyman passing the baton to another.

Newcastle’s sound form with their new model team this season has been based on searing pace and their ability on the counter whether with runners, in the case of Anthony Elanga, or with long diagonals against Tottenham that ripped a hole in the left side of their defence. Leeds rallied from being overrun by Brentford at half-time in their last home game to switch from three at the back to four and wrest back the initiative and while they reverted for the Brighton draw, in both games it was the introduction of Ao Tanaka in midfield that gave them control.

It is genuinely hard to decide whether the 6-3 defeat by Chelsea in the Carabao Cup from being 2-0 up at Stamford Bridge is significant to Leeds league form. One simplistic way of looking at it would be to say Leeds reserves were better than Chelsea’s reserves in the first half and Chelsea’s first-team were better than Leeds reserves and their shaky, debutant keeper in the second. But any similar defensive frailties tonight and there will be jitters over the next week before the international break. Newcastle, by contrast, toiled in their 1-0 victory over Millwall but the result glosses over a lack of incision for long spells of it.

Joe Rodon is out for Leeds for at least another month while Newcastle have changed to withholding information about their treatment room under Matthias Jaissle who says that it should be ‘confidential’. We do know that Joelinton, William Osula and Dan Burn are likely to still be out given the nature of their injuries but Amar Dedic, who came off at half-time at the New Den with a thigh or hamstring problem, may be back.

#1561. Spalletti open to 3-4-2-1 at Genoa but expects few changes with Napoli next

Luciano Spalletti is ready to shift from a 3-5-2 to a 3-4-2-1 at Genoa, with Alajbegovic among the options behind the striker. With eight players injured and Napoli due on Sunday, he expects his team to stay broadly the same.

Luciano Spalletti is ready to tweak his shape at Genoa without tearing up his team. On the eve of the trip, the Juventus coach said one very small positional change turns the 3-5-2 into a 3-4-2-1. Anyone, he added, can fill the two roles behind the striker.

He named Alajbegovic, Boga and Zhegrova as options in that zone. Kolo Muani was his example of the profile he has in mind. Spalletti said the forward can play partly as a number 10 and partly as a wide forward. Sarr has recovered and is available.

Tuttosport expects Alajbegovic to possibly replace Kolo Muani behind Woltemade, and sees Cambiaso as the only left-flank option with Celik injured.

The fixture list explains the caution. The trip to Genoa is the first of two games in five days. Spalletti is weighing a few rotations partly because of the second of those games, Sky Sport reported. Asked about Napoli, the coach said everything has to be taken into account. He still expects the team to stay broadly the same.

Spalletti also said his players are fully focused and have the right mentality. That follows a mixed run. Juventus lost at home to Lazio on 18 October. Afterwards Spalletti said his side had shown fragility that starts in the mind. He added that tactical systems change nothing without hunger, passion, courage and character. A draw with Rennes followed.

The win at Lecce began to make up for both results. McKennie volleyed in a Douglas Luiz free kick in the 29th minute. Douglas Luiz added the second four minutes before half-time.

Spalletti described Genoa as an extremely hard opponent, citing both the atmosphere at their ground and their tactics. He warned they can use their physical strength at set pieces and also run in behind defences. Above all, he said, the side carries Daniele De Rossi’s fighting spirit.

The warning on dead balls fits recent meetings between the clubs. Six of the last ten goals between the clubs came from set pieces: two from corners, one from a throw-in and three from penalties.

🗣️ "We must put in convincing performances"

Luciano Spalletti looks ahead to #GenoaJuve in his pre-match press conference ⤵️

🗞️ https://t.co/r2x4ICLz15 pic.twitter.com/tWcJLMx0Ia

— JuventusFC 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@juventusfcen) October 27, 2026

History still favours Juventus. They have lost only one of their last 12 Serie A games against Genoa, with nine wins and two draws. They have also won the last four. That lone defeat was 2-1 at the Ferraris on 6 May 2022. Juventus have scored 233 goals against Genoa, more than any other club in the league.

After Genoa, Juventus host Massimiliano Allegri’s Napoli in Serie A Matchday 10 on Sunday 1 November, with kick-off at 20:45.

#1560. Crawley Town vs Brentford U21 - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 09 Nov 2026 00:18

A spot in the EFL Trophy's round of 32 is up for grabs at Broadfield Stadium, when Crawley Town host Brentford U21 for their final showdown in Southern Group H on Tuesday.

The Red Devils are hoping to bounce back after a humiliating cup exit, while the Bees are searching for their third win in four games.

Crawley sacked Colin Kazim-Richards last month, leaving former Leeds United and Sheffield United manager Kevin Blackwell in interim charge until a replacement can be appointed.

The 67-year-old has collected four points from his two league matches in the dugout, drawing 1-1 with Tranmere Rovers before beating Oldham Athletic 1-0 on October 31.

That latest success has seen the Red Devils build up a tally of nine points in League Two, though they remain at the bottom of the table, three points short of 22nd-placed Rotherham United, having played two games fewer.

The only negative from Blackwell's tenure to date was the 2-0 FA Cup elimination at the hands of Southern Premier South club Wimborne Town on Sunday.

In the EFL Trophy, Crawley sit second in Southern Group H, level on points with their opponents but armed with the knowledge that a draw would likely be enough to see them through to the round of 32, owing to their six-superior goal-difference.

Blackwell's side will be desperate to avoid what would be another demoralising cup exit after seemingly turning a corner in League Two, and they will be buoyed by playing on home turf, where the hosts beat Bromley 4-0 in the EFL Trophy on October 6.

Meanwhile, Sam Saunders's Brentford U21 arrive in commendable form and ready for the challenge of facing senior professionals once again, having won two of their last three outings.

The Bees beat Bournemouth U21 4-3 in a dramatic Premier League 2 showdown on October 26, and built on that triumph with a 2-1 victory over Wycombe Wanderers U21 in the Premier League Cup.

However, Saunders's youngsters were downed 2-0 by Wolverhampton Wanderers U21 on Friday, failing to find the back of the net for the first time in eight games.

That defeat has left Brentford U21 14th in the Premier League 2 table with nine points from seven matches, winning three and losing four of their fixtures, and notably both scoring and conceding 15 goals.

The Bees were hammered 7-1 by group leaders MK Dons last time out in the EFL Trophy, and everyone involved in the club's youth setup will be pushing to prevent a second consecutive thrashing in the competition.

Crawley could name a similar lineup to the one that faced Wimborne in the FA Cup, with Danilo Orsi-Dadomo up top, supported by a trio consisting of Stephen Duke-McKenna, Kai Jennings and Dylan Morgan.

Charlie Barker could start at the base of midfield, operating alongside Jude Arthurs just in front of centre-backs Priestley Farquharson and Johnny Russell.

As for Brentford U21, they will be without senior attacker Fabio Carvalho - who featured in the 1-0 win over Bromley - due to a knock, while 19-year-old striker Kaye Furo is recovering from surgery on a foot injury.

In their absence, Isaac Holland should lead the line, and is likely to be aided by Ollie Shield, Jacob Hanson and Gustavo Nunes.

Elsewhere, midfielder Antoni Milambo is sidelined after suffering a minor setback following a brief return from his cruciate ligament injury, so Riley Owen and Kiefer Gorman look set to start in the Bees' double pivot.

Mannone; Gordon, Farquharson, Russell, Richards; Barker, Arthurs; Duke-McKenna, Jennings, Morgan; Orsi-Dadomo

Rose; Wheeler-Henry, Avenell, Grey, Picotto; Gorman, Owen; Shield, Hanson, Gustavo Nunes; Holland

Crawley will be optimistic given they are facing a youth side, but fans will be wary after seeing their team stunned by a Southern Premier South club in the FA Cup.

Brentford U21 may be fearful after receiving a thrashing last time out in the EFL Trophy, but if their youngsters can settle their nerves, then progression could be on the cards.

#1559. Man City are not a team in Enzo Maresca's ideal image yet - their imperfections are clear as win at Leipzig shows they're learning on the job, writes JACK GAUGHAN

Published: 17:30 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EDT, 5 November 2026

Watching Manchester City is not exactly straightforward at the moment. Downright confusing most of the time. Different tweaks on the same tactical theme each week, City learning on the job under new management.

Enzo Maresca recently revealed that he would rather win games 1-0 than these helter-skelter, drama-filled, error-strewn goal fests but they are not yet capable of producing that. And the players know it.

On leading in Saxony, secured by Castello Lukeba's own goal, Maresca called for Phil Foden and Abdukodir Khusanov to sprint for the bench to receive detailed instructions. As they did, Marc Guehi and Enzo Fernandez engaged in deep conversation. Gesturing arms as Erling Haaland and Elliot Anderson spoke while walking back to halfway.

The body language was as if they had gone behind. Strangely, that might encourage the boss. They know this all can improve drastically in a quest to become more cohesive. There is definitely the talent among the squad to possess a certainty of how to emphatically dominate games like this one.

None of this is particularly different to when they went on the seven-game winning run to fly out of the blocks in the Premier League, imperfections making them eminently watchable but not a team in Maresca's ideal image yet. Not by a long shot.

Later, when Anderson and Rayan Cherki were locked in debate about how to press from a goal kick, it served as a reminder of Maresca's words that this is a fresh project and change takes time. Chinks exist.

Erling Haaland came to Manchester City's rescue once more with the winning goal at Leipzig

He slid home City's winner with minutes remaining after fine work from Elliot Anderson (left)

Yet on the surface this presentable a creditable result, won by Haaland with 12 minutes left as they nestle inside the Champions League's top eight. All good for now, although added confusion comes in how little this could all mean amid an appeal of the independent commission's findings. Nobody is dissecting Maresca's evolving masterplan if they lose in court.

'We need to step up,' said Haaland, captain for the night. 'Keeping the ball, knowing when to keep it and when to go, working together offensively and defensively.'

Maresca himself admitted to shaking up the midfield and back four because he is feeling out a best XI, one he can rely upon and one that mixes that quintessentially City dominance and a more direct attacking line that can punish in a nanosecond.

'I need to understand more things about the players,' he said. 'That's why I'm so confident because I'm sure that we're going to be better and better.'

Coached by one of the Italian's closest friends and former City centre-half Martin Demichelis, Leipzig felt they deserved more. They went behind in unfortunate circumstances, although Enzo Fernandez lurked at the back post to do the honours from Nico O'Reilly's drilled cross had Lukeba not completed the job for him.

And Gianluigi Donnarumma was offering encouragement, almost embarrassed by Antonio Nusa's shot squirting through his fingers. Among other opportunities, Christoph Baumgartner curled wide from the box's edge. Baumgartner had oceans to himself amid a vacant City midfield. Anderson had gone to put out a fire out wide, vacating his holding position.

Anderson was operating there alone on the night, not something he has done regularly since a £116million summer switch, and it presented yet another iteration of Maresca's City as he attempts to locate the perfect formula.

Then two minutes summing up Donnarumma. Full stretch to acrobatically tip another Baumgartner shot wide seconds after the restart. And yet, shortly after, suffering one of those moments that are becoming far too common.

In an entertaining game, City took the lead initially when Castello Lukeba scored an own goal

Ridle Baku (right) equalised for Leipzig just after half-time due to a Gianluigi Donnarumma error

Enzo Fernandez restored City's lead with this emphatic header after Iliman Ndiaye's cross

Antonio Nusa saw Leipzig equalise for a second time before Haaland decided the game late on

RB Leipzig (4-2-3-1): Vandevoordt 6; Baku 7 (Henrichs 74, 6), Orban 6, Lukeba 4, Raum 6; El Aynaoui 6 (Seiwald 74, 6), Baumgartner 7 (Nkunku 57, 6), Banzuzi 6; Gruda 7, Romulo 6 (Gomis 67, 6), Nusa 7 (Reitz 73, 6)

Man City (4-1-4-1): Donnarumma 5; Nunes 6 (Dias 79), Khusanov 6, Guehi 6, O'Reilly 6; Anderson 8 (Bouaddi 83); Foden 6 (Doku 64, 6), Fernandez 6 (Kovacic 83), Cherki 7, Ndiaye 7 (Allan 83); Haaland 7

Ridle Baku was the beneficiary of the goalkeeper's poor positioning, forgetting about his near post, and flashed in. Somebody of Donnarumma's standing cannot allow that to happen. He would soon fumble another Baku shot, which led to a penalty appeal.

'It is not a concern but it is a mistake,' Maresca said. 'Before that he did a save that no other keeper in the world makes. Gigio knows he was not good with the goal. He's going to do better.'

City missed plenty of chances themselves before Fernandez headed in a second from Iliman Ndiaye's whipped cross but that lead only lasted three minutes, Nusa slamming into the far corner just after the hour. 'Silly goals,' Maresca said.

City kept ploughing forward, Anderson kept driving on. Ndiaye set Anderson storming down the right and he knew the area to hit. Back post, Haaland. A wicked cross, a striker's finish. Game won. Maybe that's what they were chatting about earlier.

#1557. Spalletti apologises after Genoa defeat leaves Juventus level with Napoli on 14 points

Juventus lost 2-0 at Genoa on Serie A Matchday 9, a third league defeat in nine games that undid the good work of the win at Lecce. Napoli, the next visitors to Turin, now have the same points total.

The defeat came on 28 October 2026, with both Genoa goals arriving before half-time. Luciano Spalletti apologised to the supporters afterwards. The result came three days after a 2-0 win at Lecce on Matchday 8. That win, built on first-half goals from Weston McKennie and Douglas Luiz, now looks like a false dawn.

Genoa needed little time to break through, and Ehizibue was the man to do it. His goal ended a 504-minute run without a Genoa goal against Juventus in Serie A, going back to an Albert Gudmundsson strike on 15 December 2023, Sportmediaset reported.

Baldanzi then exposed the Juventus defence again. Scoring and setting up a goal in one Serie A match was new for Baldanzi.

Juventus’s best chance of the first half came just before the interval. Kalulu shot off target after a pass from McKennie. Spalletti sent on Edon Zhegrova and Nick Woltemade for the second half. The changes did not help, and Genoa held firm. The win moved Daniele De Rossi’s side up to 10 points.

The coach did not hide from the performance. His team were beaten in every area of the pitch and must improve physically and in their fighting spirit, Spalletti told the club’s website. In his press conference he pointed to a lack of physical impact and to lost duels.

He also noted that the level shown at Lecce had not been repeated. There had been no training session between the two matches. That short turnaround is part of his explanation.

The evening got worse elsewhere. Napoli won 4-1 at Monza, with goals from Højlund, Politano, Rafa Marín and De Bruyne. Their coach, Massimiliano Allegri, watched from the stands. He was serving a two-match ban picked up against Roma.

Spalletti described Napoli as a very strong team. Both sides sit well behind the top of the table, so the meeting carries weight for each.

#1555. Furious Martin O'Neill hits out at 'debacle' after balaclava-wearing protesters abused Celtic chiefs outside meeting

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 04:56 EDT, 5 November 2026

Celtic boss Martin O’Neill has hit out at individuals wearing balaclavas who turned up at a meeting between directors and supporters.

Staged at the Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club on Monday evening, the event afforded around 120 fans a rare chance to grill the hierarchy on the direction the club is taking.

Chief executive Michael Nicholson, finance director Chris McKay and interim chairman Brian Wilson attended — with O’Neill also venturing along after learning that it was scheduled to take place.

And while the manager was pleased to have participated in a ‘robust’ discussion, he was horrified that those executives who’d agreed to front up were abused by certain fans — believed to be ultras — who hid their faces as they congregated outside.

It’s understood that they weren’t permitted access to the meeting room itself but it was still a worrying sight amid the ongoing unrest surrounding the club, with the threat of more protests ahead of Thursday night's Europa League clash with Besiktas at Celtic Park.

The flashpoint came weeks after Dermot Desmond, the club’s largest shareholder, had tennis balls thrown at him by protesters as he participated in the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship at St Andrews.

‘There was a bit of a debacle beforehand,’ said the Northern Irishman. ‘But the meeting itself was, I think you could use the word robust, yes, firm, but very orderly questioning.

O'Neill admitted he was disappointed to see individuals wearing balaclavas outside meeting

‘(We were) trying to give the answers that (were) not necessarily what people are looking for, because I’m not so sure that will ever reach a satisfactory stage for a while anyway.

‘But, yeah, it was really interesting and an experience.

‘Was everything answered by the board and myself to their satisfaction? Well, you’d have to ask the people there at the time.

‘There was no shouting. It wasn’t like (last year’s) AGM. The shouting had taken place before the meeting, you know? I mean, you are aware that people with balaclavas came up to the thing? To me, I think that was the saddest thing.

‘Would I have ever, in any day, ever thought that Celtic fans would be clothed in balaclavas before a meeting? Even if they were disapproving of what was happening, I think that’s really disappointing.

‘I do find it hard to get my head round that kind of stuff.’

The meeting came amid speculation that the club’s forthcoming annual general meeting would be held remotely.

Last year’s AGM was cut short by then chairman, Peter Lawwell, after it was disrupted by individuals shouting and brandishing red cards.

O'Neill attended  meeting with Celtic fans in Greenock where he said questioning was robust

It’s understood, though, that the meeting will go ahead as normal in a suite at Celtic Park — with O’Neill expecting to attend.

‘That’s early December, isn’t it?’ he asked. ‘So, I would expect to be at it as a manager. I assume that Brendan (Rodgers) was (present previously), so you’d be at it.

‘If given an opportunity to answer some of the things and if they want to hear from the manager, I would have no problem.

‘I hope it’s similar to what Monday night was in terms of the questions and fairness and not falling into what it was last year.’

While no minutes were taken at the meeting in Greenock, there’s been speculation that O’Neill confirmed he’d be leaving the club in the summer — despite a one-year option remaining.

Although he didn’t confirm this on Wednesday, he said: ‘I can’t imagine anybody asking me back. Seriously, I can’t imagine that happening.

‘Listen, I didn’t come in here today to give a final word at this minute.’

#1553. Carnevali calls Juventus situation ‘not acceptable’ as squad enters retreat before Napoli

Juventus will stay together in a training retreat at the JTC Continassa from Friday 30 October until Sunday's game against Napoli, after a blunt meeting between Giovanni Carnevali, the players and Luciano Spalletti. That home fixture is now widely seen as decisive for the coach's future and the direction of the season.

A direct meeting with chief executive Giovanni Carnevali has put the Juventus players and their coach under heavy pressure before Napoli’s visit.

The trigger was the loss in Genoa. Kingsley Ehizibue struck in the 12th minute, and Tommaso Baldanzi added a second in the 28th. Spalletti apologised to the supporters afterwards. He said his side had been beaten in every area. He added that they had to raise their physical level and fighting spirit.

The squad travelled back by train overnight. The players went to the Continassa the next morning. Management spoke to them there before training. Carnevali reminded them of their responsibilities to the owners, the club and the fans. He said the coaching staff still had the club’s trust, Adnkronos reported. He also asked for a strong and concrete reaction on the pitch. With the club’s agreement, Spalletti then chose to keep the players together at the training centre until kick-off.

Clubs rarely call this kind of retreat. It shows how serious the mood is at the Continassa. The message from the top is twofold. Public backing for the coaching staff comes paired with pressure for results. That places heavy weight on a single fixture.

Both sides have four wins, two draws and three defeats from nine games, Corriere dello Sport reported. Napoli sit seventh and Juventus eighth.

The gap lies in front of goal. Napoli have scored 17 times. Juventus have managed 11. Juventus have conceded only 10, however. Those figures are consistent with a side whose problems lie more in attack than in defence. A reaction against Napoli would need goals as well as fighting spirit.

Napoli will be without their coach. Massimiliano Allegri’s two-match ban covers their league games against Monza and Juventus. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea also fined him 10,000 euros. The sanction followed his abuse of match officials and later behaviour in the changing rooms during Napoli’s 3-3 draw with Roma. Napoli first announced an appeal. Allegri later said he had decided to drop it. That leaves Juventus facing a Napoli side without Allegri in charge at a moment when their own coach is under pressure.

The last meeting between the sides in Turin, on 25 January 2026, ended in a 3-0 Juventus win at the Allianz Stadium.

Juventus host Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 1 November 2026, with kick-off at 20:45.

Bayern Munich Women will head to the French capital for Tuesday’s Women’s Champions League meeting with Paris Saint-Germain Women at the Parc des Princes.

The hosts start matchday four in sixth spot in the league phase, level on five points with their seventh-placed opponents.

PSG are sitting two points adrift of the top four after winning one and drawing two of their first three league phase games.

The French giants started out with a 1-1 draw against Real Madrid in the Spanish capital before they cruised to a 5-0 home win against Belgian side Leuven on matchday two.

PSG maintained their unbeaten league phase record with a 1-1 away draw against Manchester City, which saw Tara Elimbi net an 88th-minute equaliser not long after Bunny Shaw had opened the scoring from the penalty spot.

Paulo Cesar's charges went on to play out another 1-1 scoreline in their Premiere Ligue meeting with local rivals Paris FC before they returned to winning ways with an emphatic 4-0 victory over Le Havre on Friday, leaving them in second place in the league table.

That commanding win made it five victories without conceding across their last six competitive home games, which should inspire confidence ahead of a difficult test against Bayern.

PSG are looking to record their first European home win against Bayern since running out 4-0 winners in the second leg of a quarter-final tie in March 2017.

Like PSG, Bayern are one of eight teams yet to lose in the 2026-27 league phase after collecting five points from their first three games.

#1551. Jeff Ekhator back in Juventus group training after injury nightmare

Jeff Ekhator has finally rejoined his Juventus teammates on the training pitch. The young striker, signed from Genoa in the summer, took part in a full group session at the Continassa on Friday for the first time since a run of muscle problems that has so far kept him out of every competitive game in black and white.

His return gives Luciano Spalletti one more name to consider in a week when the squad has been kept together at the training centre ahead of Sunday’s visit of Napoli.

Juventus announced the permanent deal on 1 July, and Football Italia put the fee at €16m plus add ons. The 19 year old has barely been available since.

According to Gianluca Di Marzio, who credits Sky Sport Italia with the news, his troubles began in the very first friendly of pre-season against Basel. He recovered in time to be named in the squad for the second Serie A round against Parma, where he stayed on the bench, but broke down again a few days later and has spent roughly two further months on the sidelines.

Di Marzio describes the forward as fully recovered, and Friday’s session with the rest of the group was his first since that setback.

Jeff Ekhator signs for Juventus from Genoa on a permanent deal! ⚪️⚫️ Welcome to the club, Jeff! 🙌

Nobody should expect Ekhator to be rushed into the starting eleven after so long without match practice. Football Italia sees him more as an extra option from the bench, giving Spalletti a third centre forward alongside Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani.

That alone matters for a side that has struggled for goals. Juventus have scored 11 times in nine league games, and the 2-0 defeat at Genoa on Wednesday, covered in our report on Spalletti’s apology, left them level on 14 points with Napoli.

The timing of his comeback is notable. After the Genoa loss, chief executive Giovanni Carnevali met the players and the coach, and Spalletti then decided to keep the squad together at the training ground until kick off, as explained in our piece on the Juventus retreat.

Napoli come to the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 1 November for Matchday 10, with kick off at 20:45 local time. According to the club’s own match notes, it is the first time since April 2021 that the two sides meet on the same number of points in Serie A.

Whether Ekhator makes the matchday squad will become clear when Spalletti names his group. Either way, having a fit young striker back in training is a rare piece of good news for Juventus this week.

Sources: Gianluca Di Marzio, Football Italia, Juventus

Sergio Lattanzi has followed Juventus since the days of the Trap, when Serie A felt like the centre of the football world and the Bianconeri were its undisputed rulers. Born and raised in Turin, he developed an early obsession with the tactical patterns that made Juventus so difficult to beat, and that curiosity never left him. He watches matches with a notepad nearby and a tendency to rewind passages of play more times than anyone around him considers reasonable.

Amorim spoke to DAZN not long after the final whistle to give his assessments on what was an important win for his side but one that they made hard work of in the end, with his words via MilanNews.

A response was expected after the Europa League, and it arrived. But it’s only the beginning. What positive things do you take away from this?

“I’m proud of my players. The most important thing was to be competitive, I said it before the match. If we approach every game like this, we’re one step closer to winning them all.

“What I can say is that we can win every game, but I can’t guarantee we’ll reach that level of confidence by the end of the season. I don’t feel like we’ve got that kind of consistency yet.

“And I don’t want to say anything more than ‘we can win the next game’. Because that’s the feeling I get when I look at the team. But it depends on many things. If we’d had everyone available, we would definitely have been better in the Europa League, too.

“This run of matches has been tough for us with everything that’s happened. But I can say that if we’re competitive, then we can win every game in the league. Let’s focus on that and take it one day at a time.”

“It’s the mentality. When you’re a player, there are no off days. If you play for Milan, for these clubs, there are no off days. You can’t show up like you did on Thursday and then turn on again for Sunday. It’s not possible, it’s not something that will work.

“It’s not a physical condition, it’s a question of anxiety about defeat. If you ‘panic’ about defeat, it’s not that you’re afraid of losing, but that you know that losing is the end of the world. That’s the feeling I want my teams to have.”

How is Gonçalo Ramos’ development going? He got an assist today…

“I think it’s difficult for a striker when he doesn’t score goals. But I’ll repeat: we don’t spend much time in the final third of the pitch. We have possession, we’re improving our ball output, but we’re missing that. When we’re consistently in the final third, Gonçalo will score a lot of goals.

“It’s a team problem, we’re not helping Ramos, but he’s helping us a lot. It’s a process, a journey. And we’re not yet at the point of being so dominant that Ramos spends most of his time in the opponent’s penalty area. We’re still a long way off.”

#1548. The 'family football club' now being promoted by unlicensed gambling and an 'international adult star': Leicester City fans rage against team's choice of sponsor after two relegations

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 05:00 EDT, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 05:24 EDT, 5 November 2026

Leicester City supporters have expressed fury and dismay after the club's unlicensed gambling shirt sponsor appointed an 'international porn star' as its new ambassador.

Online casino company BC Game, who has been the Foxes' primary shirt sponsor since the start of the 2024-25 season, announced its partnership with Russian adult content creator Eva Elfie in a video on X earlier this week.

The promotional video, which was laced with innuendo and featured Elfie receiving a package from a delivery man containing her partnership contract, was accompanied with the caption: 'Welcome to BC Game Eva Elfie! Let the fun begin.'

The Foxes Trust has reacted angrily to the shirt sponsor’s association with Elfie, who has also built a following in Esports and competitive online gaming communities.

In a furious statement titled 'BC Game - It gets worse', the fan body said: 'Most Leicester City supporters will know by now the Trust's dismay and discontent with BC Game being our front of shirt sponsor.

'BC Game have now announced a new partnership with "international content creator and Esports personality" Eva Elfie... who just happens to be an international porn star.

Leicester City supporters have expressed fury and dismay after the club's unlicensed gambling shirt sponsor appointed 'international porn star' Eva Elfie as its new ambassador

Casino firm BC Game has been Leicester's primary shirt sponsor since the 2024-25 season

Welcome to BC Game @EvaElfie! Let the fun begin 😏 pic.twitter.com/xzLJ4uBOx7

'From the moment the Club decided to take sponsorship from a betting company, we felt Leicester City were ditching its values. Our first article in July 2024 said that "It doesn't feel like who LCFC are to have a gambling website on our shirts and seems to be another step away from our well run family club reputation".

'The Club has not only partnered with a gambling company, but chosen one that is unlicensed to operate in the UK, has unanswered questions about the legitimacy of its funding and its origins, and allows clients to "game" using cryptocurrencies.

'Now throw into the mix that BC Game have entered into a partnership with someone who continues to make their name via adult content.

'Both gambling and pornography can have devastating impacts on people's lives, in particular young people. Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City. Is this who we are now?

'Our end of season survey showed 73% of fans felt negative about the relationship, and only 5% were content with it.

'As always our message is, if you're purchasing an LCFC replica shirt, opt for one that doesn't have the BC Game logo on it.'

BC Game, which The Foxes Trust claim has failed to respond to questions about its funding and legitimacy, lost its UK operating licence in December 2024 and has since shifted its focus to overseas markets.

Focusing on Elfie's esports portfolio in his announcement, BC Game chief executive Ali 'Ako' Muhanned said: 'Eva has built an incredible relationship with the gaming and esports community through genuine passion and consistent content creation.

'At BC.GAME, we want to work with creators who understand how to entertain, connect with audiences in real time, and bring positive energy to our players. Her live streams are dynamic and engaging, making her a natural fit as we expand our footprint across esports and interactive entertainment.'

Elfie, who has 4.8million followers on Instagram, also released her debut single 'Fairyland' last month.

Since partnering with BC Game, the Foxes have plummeted down the football league, suffering back-to-back relegations from the Premier League to League One.

Elfie, who has 4.8million Instagram followers, is known in Esports and gaming communities too

BC Game lost its licence to operate in the UK in 2024 and now targets overseas markets

Leicester, who famously won the Premier League against all odds in 2016 and lifted the FA Cup in 2021, were docked six points for breaching spending rules during last season's dismal Championship campaign and failed to survive the drop.

Today, the East Midlands club sit 10th in League One after 13 matches, winning five, losing four and drawing four.

When the partnership was first announced in 2024, Leicester City chief executive Susan Whelan said: 'We welcome BC Game to Leicester City – an opportunity to work with an innovative partner in a new category for the Club.

'As a leading global operator in a rapidly evolving environment, BC Game already have a history of successful relationships in sport and we look forward to the development of a mutually beneficial partnership.

'The ability to attract high-value partners upon our return to the Premier League is vital to our determination to re-establish Leicester City among the game’s elite, to continue to invest in a competitive squad and to ensure the best possible experience for our supporters.'

#1547. Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town

There is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. But, my word, he does make it difficult. Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation continues to sparkle whenever he steps on to the field, and he did so again with this superb display against Ipswich Town.

"The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn

At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second showed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

Max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x

As Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a new contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.

“A joy to have him,” said Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.

“Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”

"He was brilliant, he made the difference - we need to look after him" 🌟Mikel Arteta says Arsenal need to "be really cautious" with 16-year-old Max Dowman after he scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/1msJAEkK8z

Dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. Ipswich scored a goal of their own, through Anis Mehmeti, but never seemed likely to cause the visitors too much bother. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” said Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”

Dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. His first strike for the club, against Everton last season, came after he left an opponent face-down on the turf at the Emirates Stadium. He inflicted the same pain here upon poor Cédric Kipré, who tried to tackle the teenager in the seventh minute but ended up with a mouthful of grass.

It was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. The chance came after Bruno Guimarães and Merino, majestic in midfield, had monstered Ipswich’s attempts to play out from the back. Merino was dominant throughout, winning tackles with steel and then spinning away opponents with style. “He’s unbelievable,” said Arteta.

Arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.

Given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.

The only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.

Ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.

Akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.

"He's 16 years old, and we have to be cautious of that" 💫Mikel Arteta reacts to an incredible performance from Max Dowman as Arsenal put FOUR past Ipswich 🔴Don't miss the Carabao Cup on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/AIcAbMx6ub

On managing the hype that surrounds Dowman, Arteta said: “What we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands... We need to make sure that every time we throw him in it’s in the right context with the right preparation.”

Conor Coady shares his thoughts on Arteta’s role in Dowman’s development:

"He'll know how to nurture him!" 🗣️Conor Coady says Mikel Arteta is the perfect manager for Max Dowman 👏 pic.twitter.com/YdgLxfKiOf

Asked about Dowman’s two-goal performance, Arteta said: “A joy to have him, Marli [Salmon] as well. Seventeen years old, to play at that level with the physicality they have to be able to handle that level, it’s remarkable. Max, yeah, it’s inevitable to talk about him when he scores and he creates the moments he has created tonight. It’s normal.”

He added: “He is coping better and better and better, he did the action where he regains the ball and wins it in the first goal, he loses his man... He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play on the biggest stage and still handles the situation with such naturality.”

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Mikel Arteta said: “Really pleased with a lot of things we did tonight, the way we attacked the game, how dominant, fluid and aggressive we were, right from the beginning to try to influence the result. We scored two very early goals that gave us obviously a great platform for the game.

“Individually some big performances as well. Some debuts tonight which is great to see as well, so we take a lot of positives from tonight.”

Ipswich’s substitutes have breathed some life into their attack. Akpom fires a cross-cum-shot towards goal but strikes the side-netting.

Another couple of substitutions for O’Neil, who will now be thinking about Everton next weekend. Davis and Walle Egeli are on for Ouattara and McAteer.

The record for the youngest hat-trick scorer across all professional tiers of English football belongs to Trevor Francis.

Playing for Birmingham City against Bolton Wanderers in Division Two on February 20, 1971, Francis scored four goals in a 4-0 win at just 16 years and 307 days old.

O’Neil makes a pair of changes, replacing Philogene and Flemming with Clarke and former Arsenal striker Akpom.

Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 4 (Merino) Arsenal work the ball infield from the right in instalments, Madueke feeding Zubimendi who passes through Dowman to Merino on the edge of the box who opens up his body before guiding the ball around Walton.

Arsenal are FLYING!Merino puts another goal away for the Gunners 🔥 pic.twitter.com/nrzHHk1bou

Max Dowman was first spotted by Arsenal at four years old. He’s been running past opponents and scoring goals ever since. Now he’s just doing it on the professional stage, in front of the watching world, but it still looks completely normal to him.

Chance! It could, and maybe should, have been four. Merino threads a wonderful through-ball beyond Ipswich’s final line of defence and Madueke steals in to poke the ball across the face of goal with the outside of his left boot. Gyokeres was in the middle but could not divert the ball goalwards.

Kepa stretches to claim a looped Flemming cross which had echoes of the Spaniard’s game-defining error in last year’s League Cup final. This time he collects with a minimum of fuss. That Flemming was so far out on the left will be of concern to O’Neil.

Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 3 (Dowman) Madueke picks out Zubimendi in the box who in turn finds Dowman in the right half space and he gallops on to the ball before arrowing the ball past Walton. Zubimendi gets us going again for the second 45 minutes. Konsa has replaced Gabriel at the interval.

Such is the midfielder’s versatility, his heat map tonight paints a wildly different picture to that from his 45 minutes at the Stadium of Light over the weekend. He has played the midfield-sentry role in Suffolk and has executed it well.

A flurry of chances for Ipswich. Philogene’s lopping cross is tipped away by Kepa but the ball falls to Flemming at the back post and his effort pinballs around a thicket of Arsenal limbs before reaching Florentino on the edge of the box, whose effort sails over the bar.

Max Dowman’s second goal for Arsenal is quite similar to his first, scored so thrillingly against Everton last season. On both occasions he has put an opposition defender face-first in the turf before scoring the goal. Outrageous ability with the ball at his feet.

Early indications suggest Zubimendi will play in the nominal right-back position, inverting into midfield when Arsenal build up.

Flemming gets us started. Ipswich kicking from right to left.

The players emerge from the Portman Road tunnel, Ipswich in their customary home blue shirts and white shorts, Arsenal in red and also white shorts.
